blog_summary: Adrian Colyer discusses the evolution of Twitter's Heron streaming engine from an internal system to an open-source, extensible platform. The paper highlights the challenges of transitioning Heron from a Twitter-specific system to a modular architecture that can adapt to diverse environments and workloads. The modular design allows for flexible integration with different schedulers (e.g., YARN, Aurora) and software stacks, while maintaining performance. The blog post emphasizes Heron's microkernel-inspired architecture, which separates concerns into seven self-contained modules, including resource management, scheduling, and stream handling. Colyer finds the comparisons between Heron, Storm, and Spark Streaming particularly insightful, noting Heron's superior performance (3-5x higher throughput and 2-4x lower latency than Storm) and better resource isolation. The modularity and extensibility of Heron are presented as key advantages over competitors.
